newsitem.title: MEXICO: Bancomer shares up sharply late morning.
newsitem.headline: Bancomer shares up sharply late morning.

text.p: Shares listed by Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest financial groups, were up sharply to a record levels in late morning trade on the local bourse.
Bancomer B shares were up 32 centavos to 5.20 pesos, below an earlier high of 5.32 pesos but still above the previous trading record of 4.89 pesos.

Dealers said they were buying because a sharp fall in domestic interest rates on Tuesday would tend to ease the banking division's past-due loans portfolio and on a mortgage debt restructuring plan that was to be unveiled on Wednesday.

"Short-term trading patterns are very much influenced by interest rates...and foreign buyers tend to go for the big names in financial stocks," said Robert Lacousiere, a financial sector analyst at Santander Investment-Mexico.

Banco de Mexico placed bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at 17.70 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction, a fall of 102 basis points since last week to their lowest level since the December 1994 peso devaluation crisis.
Lacousiere nonetheless said the rise in share price was not fundamentally sound.
"We think the market has overshot on this...if anything, the mortgage program shows asset quality is still poor," he added.
